description.value: The study investigated how FTO rs9939609 genotype relates to circulating acyl-ghrelin and neural responses to food cues in normal-weight AA and TT humans.
A randomized crossover fMRI study compared fasted and fed states in adiposity-matched AA and TT male subjects.

name.value: Positive relationship between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response in the TT group

definition.value: A positive relationship between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response to high-calorie versus low-calorie food images in the TT group.

value: In TT subjects, there was a positive relationship between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response, whereas in AA subjects, a negative relationship was found.
These findings suggest that the FTO genotype alters CNS responsivity to acyl-ghrelin in the fasted state.

name.value: Negative relationship between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response in the AA group

definition.value: A negative relationship between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response to high-calorie versus low-calorie food images in the AA group.

value: In AA subjects, a negative relationship was found between circulating acyl-ghrelin and BOLD response, whereas in TT subjects, there was a positive relationship.
These findings suggest that the FTO genotype alters CNS responsivity to acyl-ghrelin in the fasted state.

name.value: Differential relationship between postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression and BOLD response in the cuneus

definition.value: The relationship between food-related BOLD response and postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression differed between AA and TT subjects.

value: Neural responses to all food images within the occipitotemporal portion of the fusiform gyrus, the postcentral gyrus, and the cuneus were differentially sensitive to postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression in the AA and TT subjects.

This effect was driven by a positive relationship between the BOLD response within these regions and meal-induced acyl-ghrelin suppression in the TT subjects, while the AA subjects displayed a negative relationship.

name.value: Divergent relationship between BOLD response and postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression in the right caudate nucleus

definition.value: The relationship between BOLD response to hedonic food images and postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression differed between AA and TT subjects in the right caudate nucleus.

value: In response to high-calorie images, the AA and TT subjects exhibited a significantly divergent response within the right caudate nucleus.
In AA subjects, the BOLD response within the caudate was positively related with postprandial acyl-ghrelin suppression, whereas in TT subjects, a negative relationship was observed.
